    11	/-!
    12	# Chart-module structure of the m-chart glued sheaf (DAT-1, stage 1c)
    13	
    14	The `Γ(X, V)`-module and coefficient-ring properties of the glued section module
    15	`F(V)` on an affine chart `V` carrying a finite subordinate trivializing basic-open
    16	family (`informal/spec-dat-1.md`, decision (D5)): sections `h : ι → Γ(X, V)` whose
    17	basic opens `D(h i)` lie in gluing pieces (`hP : D(h i) ≤ U (σ i)`) and span the unit
    18	ideal (`hspan : Ideal.span (Set.range h) = ⊤` — the worksheet partition witness feeds
    19	this through `Ideal.span_range_eq_top_of_sum_eq_one`).
    20	
    21	All statements are relative to an ambient packaging
    22	`[Scheme.QcohOn (gluedSheaf k U g) V]` whose action is componentwise (the hypothesis
    23	`hq`, discharged by `rfl` for packagings built by `gluedQcohOn` — the same interface as
    24	`gluedPairData`), with the chart module structure `Scheme.QcohOn.moduleOfLE` bound by
    25	`letI` in statements (RE-0 pattern) and the section modules in the sheaf-object
    26	spelling `(gluedSheaf k U g).obj.obj (op W)` — the spelling the engine consumes.
    27	
    28	* `gluedPieceModule`/`gluedPieceEquiv` — each piece `F(D(h i))` is a free rank-one
    29	  `Γ(X, D(h i))`-module through the piece trivialization `gluedTriv`;
    30	* `isUnit_algebraMap_end_glued` — a chart section restricting to a unit acts invertibly
    31	  on the glued sections of an open below a piece (trivialization conjugation);
    32	* `isLocalizedModule_secResₗ_glued` — **the RE-0 bridge fired per piece**:
    33	  `F(V) → F(D(h i))` is an `IsLocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers (h i))` (the abstract
    34	  bridge at `V ⊓ D(h i)`, transported across the opens equality `V ⊓ D(h i) = D(h i)`
    35	  by `IsLocalizedModule.of_linearEquiv`);
    36	* the localization-local chart properties: `moduleFinite_glued`,
    37	  `finitePresentation_glued`, `flat_glued`, `projective_glued` (over `Γ(X, V)`), and
    38	  the coefficient-ring transports `flat_glued_of_flat` (under `Module.Flat k Γ(X, V)` —
    39	  a benign weakening of the spec's freeness hypothesis: free ⟹ flat) and
    40	  `projective_glued_of_free` (under `Module.Free k Γ(X, V)`);
    41	* `moduleFinite_aeval'_glued` — the `AEval'`-finiteness export: an endomorphism acting
    42	  as the packaged action of a chart coordinate `a₀` has `k[X]`-finite chart lattice
    43	  whenever `Scheme.mulSectionEnd k a₀` does (the landed E-i input), through
    44	  `RigidEngine.moduleFinite_aeval'_of_smul_finite` and `moduleFinite_glued`.
    45	-/
    46	
    47	set_option autoImplicit false
    48	
    49	universe u
    50	
    51	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite TopologicalSpace Polynomial
    52	
    53	/-! ## A partition of unity spans the unit ideal -/
    54	
    55	/-- **Span-⊤ from a partition of unity**: if `∑ i, a i * h i = 1` in a commutative ring,
    56	the range of `h` generates the unit ideal. -/
    57	theorem Ideal.span_range_eq_top_of_sum_eq_one {A : Type u} [CommRing A] {ι : Type*}
    58	    [Fintype ι] (a h : ι → A) (hpart : ∑ i, a i * h i = 1) :
    59	    Ideal.span (Set.range h) = ⊤ := by
    60	  rw [Ideal.eq_top_iff_one, ← hpart]
    61	  exact Ideal.sum_mem _ fun i _ =>
    62	    Ideal.mul_mem_left _ _ (Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_range_self i))
    63	
    64	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    65	
    66	section Module
    67	
    68	variable (k : Type u) [CommRing k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    69	
    70	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule
    71	
    72	variable {J : Type u} (U : J → X.Opens) (g : ∀ i j : J, Γ(X, U i ⊓ U j)ˣ)
    73	
    74	/-! ## Restriction bookkeeping -/
    75	
    76	/-- Componentwise restriction composes. -/
    77	lemma gluedRes_gluedRes {W'' W' W : X.Opens} (h₁ : W'' ≤ W') (h₂ : W' ≤ W)
    78	    (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule k U g W)) :
    79	    gluedRes k U g h₁ (gluedRes k U g h₂ s) = gluedRes k U g (h₁.trans h₂) s :=
    80	  Subtype.ext (funext fun _ => by
    81	    simp only [gluedRes_coe, Scheme.resHom_resHom])
    82	
    83	/-- Componentwise restriction along `W ≤ W` is the identity. -/
    84	lemma gluedRes_self {W : X.Opens} (hW : W ≤ W) (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule k U g W)) :
    85	    gluedRes k U g hW s = s :=
    86	  Subtype.ext (funext fun _ => Scheme.resHom_self _ _)
    87	
    88	/-! ## The coefficient action of a structure-morphism scalar -/
    89	
    90	/-- The componentwise action of the image `X.overAlgebraMap k V c` of a coefficient
    91	`c : k` agrees with the `k`-module action on glued sections. -/
    92	lemma gluedQsmul_overAlgebraMap {V W : X.Opens} (hWV : W ≤ V) (c : k)
    93	    (m : ↥(gluedSubmodule k U g W)) :
    94	    gluedQsmul k U g hWV (X.overAlgebraMap k V c) m = c • m := by
    95	  refine Subtype.ext (funext fun j => ?_)
    96	  have hc : (c • m).val j = c • m.val j := rfl
    97	  rw [gluedQsmul_coe, hc, Scheme.overModule_smul_def]
    98	  congr 1
    99	  exact X.overAlgebraMap_apply_res k (homOfLE (inf_le_left.trans hWV)).op c
   100	
   101	variable {V : X.Opens} {ι : Type u} {σ : ι → J} {h : ι → Γ(X, V)}
   102	
   103	/-! ## The piece module structure -/
   104	
   105	/-- **The `Aᵢ := Γ(X, D(h i))`-module structure on a piece** `Mᵢ := F(D(h i))`,
   106	transported through the `k`-linear piece trivialization `tᵢ : Mᵢ ≃ₗ[k] Γ(X, D(h i))`:
   107	`a • m := tᵢ⁻¹ (a * tᵢ m)`. This makes `Mᵢ` free of rank one over `Aᵢ`
   108	(`gluedPieceEquiv`). -/
   109	@[reducible] noncomputable def gluedPieceModule (hc : Scheme.IsGluingCocycle U g)
   110	    (hP : ∀ i : ι, X.basicOpen (h i) ≤ U (σ i)) (i : ι) :
   111	    Module Γ(X, X.basicOpen (h i)) ↥(gluedSubmodule k U g (X.basicOpen (h i))) where
   112	  smul a m := (gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)).symm (a * gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i) m)
   113	  one_smul m := by
   114	    change (gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)).symm (1 * gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i) m) = m
   115	    rw [one_mul, LinearEquiv.symm_apply_apply]
   116	  mul_smul a b m := by
   117	    change (gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)).symm (a * b * gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i) m) =
   118	      (gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)).symm
   119	        (a * gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)
   120	          ((gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)).symm (b * gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i) m)))
   121	    rw [LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply, mul_assoc]
   122	  smul_zero a := by
   123	    change (gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)).symm (a * gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i) 0) = 0
   124	    rw [map_zero, mul_zero, map_zero]
   125	  smul_add a m n := by
   126	    change (gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)).symm (a * gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i) (m + n)) =
   127	      (gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)).symm (a * gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i) m) +
   128	        (gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)).symm (a * gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i) n)
   129	    rw [map_add, mul_add, map_add]
   130	  add_smul a b m := by
   131	    change (gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)).symm ((a + b) * gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i) m) =
   132	      (gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)).symm (a * gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i) m) +
   133	        (gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)).symm (b * gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i) m)
   134	    rw [add_mul, map_add]
   135	  zero_smul m := by
   136	    change (gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)).symm (0 * gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i) m) = 0
   137	    rw [zero_mul, map_zero]
   138	
   139	lemma gluedPieceModule_smul_def (hc : Scheme.IsGluingCocycle U g)
   140	    (hP : ∀ i : ι, X.basicOpen (h i) ≤ U (σ i)) (i : ι)
   141	    (a : Γ(X, X.basicOpen (h i))) (m : ↥(gluedSubmodule k U g (X.basicOpen (h i)))) :
   142	    letI := gluedPieceModule k U g hc hP i
   143	    a • m = (gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)).symm (a * gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i) m) :=
   144	  rfl
   145	
   146	/-- **Each piece is `Aᵢ`-free of rank one**: the piece trivialization `tᵢ`, promoted to
   147	an `Aᵢ`-linear equivalence `Mᵢ ≃ₗ[Aᵢ] Aᵢ` for the `gluedPieceModule` structure. -/
   148	noncomputable def gluedPieceEquiv (hc : Scheme.IsGluingCocycle U g)
   149	    (hP : ∀ i : ι, X.basicOpen (h i) ≤ U (σ i)) (i : ι) :
   150	    letI := gluedPieceModule k U g hc hP i
   151	    ↥(gluedSubmodule k U g (X.basicOpen (h i))) ≃ₗ[Γ(X, X.basicOpen (h i))]
   152	      Γ(X, X.basicOpen (h i)) :=
   153	  letI := gluedPieceModule k U g hc hP i
   154	  { toFun := gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)
   155	    map_add' := (gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)).map_add
   156	    map_smul' := fun a m => by
   157	      change gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)
   158	          ((gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)).symm (a * gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i) m)) =
   159	        a • gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i) m
   160	      rw [LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply, smul_eq_mul]
   161	    invFun := (gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)).symm
   162	    left_inv := (gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)).left_inv
   163	    right_inv := (gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)).right_inv }
   164	
   165	@[simp]
   166	lemma gluedPieceEquiv_apply (hc : Scheme.IsGluingCocycle U g)
   167	    (hP : ∀ i : ι, X.basicOpen (h i) ≤ U (σ i)) (i : ι)
   168	    (m : ↥(gluedSubmodule k U g (X.basicOpen (h i)))) :
   169	    gluedPieceEquiv k U g hc hP i m = gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i) m :=
   170	  rfl
   171	
   172	@[simp]
   173	lemma gluedPieceEquiv_symm_apply (hc : Scheme.IsGluingCocycle U g)
   174	    (hP : ∀ i : ι, X.basicOpen (h i) ≤ U (σ i)) (i : ι)
   175	    (t : Γ(X, X.basicOpen (h i))) :
   176	    (gluedPieceEquiv k U g hc hP i).symm t = (gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)).symm t :=
   177	  rfl
   178	
   179	/-- **The piece `Aᵢ`-action restricted along `A → Aᵢ` is the chart action**: for
   180	`r : Γ(X, V)`, the `Aᵢ`-scalar `X.resHom … r` acts on `Mᵢ` as the componentwise chart
   181	action `gluedQsmul`. -/
   182	lemma gluedPieceModule_smul_resHom (hc : Scheme.IsGluingCocycle U g)
   183	    (hP : ∀ i : ι, X.basicOpen (h i) ≤ U (σ i)) (i : ι) (r : Γ(X, V))
   184	    (m : ↥(gluedSubmodule k U g (X.basicOpen (h i)))) :
   185	    letI := gluedPieceModule k U g hc hP i
   186	    (X.resHom (X.basicOpen_le (h i)) r) • m =
   187	      gluedQsmul k U g (X.basicOpen_le (h i)) r m := by
   188	  letI := gluedPieceModule k U g hc hP i
   189	  apply (gluedTriv k hc (σ i) (hP i)).injective
   190	  rw [gluedTriv_gluedQsmul k U g hc, gluedPieceModule_smul_def,
   191	    LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply]
   192	
   193	/-! ## The packaged chart module structure: scalar towers and the RE-0 bridge -/
   194	
   195	section Packaged
   196	
   197	variable [Scheme.QcohOn (gluedSheaf k U g) V]
   198	
   199	/-- `IsScalarTower k Γ(X, V) F(W)` for any `W ≤ V`: the coefficient action of the
   200	packaging factors through the structure map `k → Γ(X, V)`. -/
   201	lemma isScalarTower_coeff
   202	    (hq : ∀ {W : X.Opens} (hW : W ≤ V) (r : Γ(X, V)) (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule k U g W)),
   203	      Scheme.QcohOn.qsmul (F := gluedSheaf k U g) hW r s = gluedQsmul k U g hW r s)
   204	    {W : X.Opens} (hWV : W ≤ V) :
   205	    letI : Module Γ(X, V) ↥(gluedSubmodule k U g W) :=
   206	      Scheme.QcohOn.moduleOfLE (F := gluedSheaf k U g) hWV
   207	    letI : Algebra k Γ(X, V) := (X.overAlgebraMap k V).toAlgebra
   208	    IsScalarTower k Γ(X, V) ↥(gluedSubmodule k U g W) := by
   209	  letI : Module Γ(X, V) ↥(gluedSubmodule k U g W) :=
   210	    Scheme.QcohOn.moduleOfLE (F := gluedSheaf k U g) hWV
   211	  letI : Algebra k Γ(X, V) := (X.overAlgebraMap k V).toAlgebra
   212	  refine IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_smul fun c m => ?_
   213	  change Scheme.QcohOn.qsmul (F := gluedSheaf k U g) hWV (X.overAlgebraMap k V c) m
   214	    = c • m
   215	  rw [hq hWV (X.overAlgebraMap k V c) m]
   216	  exact gluedQsmul_overAlgebraMap k U g hWV c m
   217	
   218	/-- `IsScalarTower Γ(X, V) Γ(X, D(h i)) Mᵢ`: the packaged chart action factors through
   219	the restriction `Γ(X, V) → Γ(X, D(h i))` and the piece module structure. -/
   220	lemma isScalarTower_chart_piece (hc : Scheme.IsGluingCocycle U g)
   221	    (hq : ∀ {W : X.Opens} (hW : W ≤ V) (r : Γ(X, V)) (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule k U g W)),
   222	      Scheme.QcohOn.qsmul (F := gluedSheaf k U g) hW r s = gluedQsmul k U g hW r s)
   223	    (hP : ∀ i : ι, X.basicOpen (h i) ≤ U (σ i)) (i : ι) :
   224	    letI := gluedPieceModule k U g hc hP i
   225	    letI : Module Γ(X, V) ↥(gluedSubmodule k U g (X.basicOpen (h i))) :=
   226	      Scheme.QcohOn.moduleOfLE (F := gluedSheaf k U g) (X.basicOpen_le (h i))
   227	    IsScalarTower Γ(X, V) Γ(X, X.basicOpen (h i))
   228	      ↥(gluedSubmodule k U g (X.basicOpen (h i))) := by
   229	  letI := gluedPieceModule k U g hc hP i
   230	  letI : Module Γ(X, V) ↥(gluedSubmodule k U g (X.basicOpen (h i))) :=
   231	    Scheme.QcohOn.moduleOfLE (F := gluedSheaf k U g) (X.basicOpen_le (h i))
   232	  refine IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_smul fun r m => ?_
   233	  change (X.resHom (X.basicOpen_le (h i)) r) • m =
   234	    Scheme.QcohOn.qsmul (F := gluedSheaf k U g) (X.basicOpen_le (h i)) r m
   235	  rw [hq (X.basicOpen_le (h i)) r m]
   236	  exact gluedPieceModule_smul_resHom k U g hc hP i r m
   237	
   238	/-- **Invertibility of the packaged action of a unit**: a chart section `r` restricting
   239	to a unit on an open `W` below a gluing piece acts invertibly on `F(W)` — the action is
   240	conjugate, through the piece trivialization, to multiplication by the unit `r↾_W`. This
   241	discharges the `map_units` hypothesis of the RE-0 bridge. -/
   242	lemma isUnit_algebraMap_end_glued (hc : Scheme.IsGluingCocycle U g)
   243	    (hq : ∀ {W : X.Opens} (hW : W ≤ V) (r : Γ(X, V)) (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule k U g W)),
   244	      Scheme.QcohOn.qsmul (F := gluedSheaf k U g) hW r s = gluedQsmul k U g hW r s)
   245	    {W : X.Opens} (hWV : W ≤ V) {j : J} (hWj : W ≤ U j) (r : Γ(X, V))
   246	    (hr : IsUnit (X.resHom hWV r)) :
   247	    letI := Scheme.QcohOn.moduleOfLE (F := gluedSheaf k U g) hWV
   248	    IsUnit (algebraMap Γ(X, V)
   249	      (Module.End Γ(X, V) ((gluedSheaf k U g).obj.obj (op W))) r) := by
   250	  letI := Scheme.QcohOn.moduleOfLE (F := gluedSheaf k U g) hWV
   251	  have hE : ⇑(algebraMap Γ(X, V)
   252	      (Module.End Γ(X, V) ((gluedSheaf k U g).obj.obj (op W))) r) =
   253	      fun m : ↥(gluedSubmodule k U g W) => gluedQsmul k U g hWV r m := by
   254	    funext m
   255	    rw [Module.algebraMap_end_apply]
   256	    exact hq hWV r m
   257	  rw [Module.End.isUnit_iff, hE]
   258	  obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := hr
   259	  refine Function.bijective_iff_has_inverse.mpr
   260	    ⟨fun m => (gluedTriv k hc j hWj).symm
   261	      ((↑v⁻¹ : Γ(X, W)) * gluedTriv k hc j hWj m), fun m => ?_, fun m => ?_⟩
   262	  · change (gluedTriv k hc j hWj).symm
   263	      ((↑v⁻¹ : Γ(X, W)) * gluedTriv k hc j hWj (gluedQsmul k U g hWV r m)) = m
   264	    rw [gluedTriv_gluedQsmul k U g hc hWV hWj r m, ← hv, Units.inv_mul_cancel_left,
   265	      LinearEquiv.symm_apply_apply]
   266	  · change gluedQsmul k U g hWV r
   267	      ((gluedTriv k hc j hWj).symm ((↑v⁻¹ : Γ(X, W)) * gluedTriv k hc j hWj m)) = m
   268	    apply (gluedTriv k hc j hWj).injective
   269	    rw [gluedTriv_gluedQsmul k U g hc hWV hWj, LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply, ← hv,
   270	      Units.mul_inv_cancel_left]
   271	
   272	/-- **The RE-0 bridge fired on a piece** (DAT-1 (1c)): on an affine chart `V`, the
   273	restriction `F(V) → F(D(h i))` exhibits the piece sections as the localization of the
   274	chart sections at the powers of `h i`. The abstract bridge
   275	(`Scheme.QcohOn.isLocalizedModule_secResₗ`) produces this at `V ⊓ D(h i)` — its
   276	`map_units` hypothesis is the trivialization conjugation `isUnit_algebraMap_end_glued` —
   277	and `IsLocalizedModule.of_linearEquiv` transports across the opens equality
   278	`V ⊓ D(h i) = D(h i)`. -/
   279	theorem isLocalizedModule_secResₗ_glued (hV : IsAffineOpen V)
   280	    (hc : Scheme.IsGluingCocycle U g)
   281	    (hq : ∀ {W : X.Opens} (hW : W ≤ V) (r : Γ(X, V)) (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule k U g W)),
   282	      Scheme.QcohOn.qsmul (F := gluedSheaf k U g) hW r s = gluedQsmul k U g hW r s)
   283	    (hP : ∀ i : ι, X.basicOpen (h i) ≤ U (σ i)) (i : ι) :
   284	    letI := Scheme.QcohOn.moduleOfLE (F := gluedSheaf k U g) (le_refl V)
   285	    letI := Scheme.QcohOn.moduleOfLE (F := gluedSheaf k U g) (X.basicOpen_le (h i))
   286	    IsLocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers (h i))
   287	      (Scheme.QcohOn.secResₗ (F := gluedSheaf k U g)
   288	        (X.basicOpen_le (h i)) (le_refl V)) := by
   289	  letI := Scheme.QcohOn.moduleOfLE (F := gluedSheaf k U g) (le_refl V)
   290	  letI := Scheme.QcohOn.moduleOfLE (F := gluedSheaf k U g) (X.basicOpen_le (h i))
   291	  letI := Scheme.QcohOn.moduleOfLE (F := gluedSheaf k U g)
   292	    (inf_le_left : V ⊓ X.basicOpen (h i) ≤ V)
   293	  -- the unit-action hypothesis on `V ⊓ D(h i)`, an open below the piece `U (σ i)`
   294	  have hru : IsUnit (X.resHom (inf_le_left : V ⊓ X.basicOpen (h i) ≤ V) (h i)) := by
   295	    have h1 : IsUnit (X.resHom (X.basicOpen_le (h i)) (h i)) :=
   296	      X.toRingedSpace.isUnit_res_basicOpen (h i)
   297	    have h2 : X.resHom (inf_le_left : V ⊓ X.basicOpen (h i) ≤ V) (h i) =
   298	        X.resHom (inf_le_right : V ⊓ X.basicOpen (h i) ≤ X.basicOpen (h i))
   299	          (X.resHom (X.basicOpen_le (h i)) (h i)) := by
   300	      rw [Scheme.resHom_resHom]
   301	    rw [h2]
   302	    exact (X.resHom
   303	      (inf_le_right : V ⊓ X.basicOpen (h i) ≤ X.basicOpen (h i))).isUnit_map h1
   304	  -- the abstract bridge at `V ⊓ D(h i)`
   305	  haveI hbridge := Scheme.QcohOn.isLocalizedModule_secResₗ (F := gluedSheaf k U g)
   306	    hV (h i)
   307	    (isUnit_algebraMap_end_glued k U g hc hq
   308	      (inf_le_left : V ⊓ X.basicOpen (h i) ≤ V)
   309	      (inf_le_right.trans (hP i)) (h i) hru)

     9	/-!
    10	# The m-chart cocycle-glued sheaf (DAT-1, stage 1a)
    11	
    12	For a scheme `X` over `Spec k`, a family of opens `U : J → X.Opens` and **transition
    13	multipliers** `g i j ∈ Γ(X, U i ⊓ U j)ˣ`, the glued sheaf of `informal/spec-dat-1.md`
    14	(the m-chart generalization of the two-chart `AlgebraicGeometry.twistSheaf`), as a sheaf
    15	of `k`-modules on the small Zariski site of `X`:
    16	`F_g(W) = {s ∈ Π j, Γ(W ⊓ U j) | s i = g i j · s j on W ⊓ U i ⊓ U j for all i, j}`
    17	(`AlgebraicGeometry.gluedSheaf`), together with
    18	
    19	* the **cocycle law** `Scheme.IsGluingCocycle` (`g i i = 1` and
    20	  `g i j · g j l = g i l` on triple overlaps) — a `Prop`-structure: the carrier needs no
    21	  law (the matching relation is restriction-stable for arbitrary multipliers), the
    22	  trivializations consume it;
    23	* the **piece trivializations** `F_g(W) ≃ₗ[k] Γ(X, W)` for `W ≤ U j`, given by the
    24	  `j`-th component (`AlgebraicGeometry.gluedTriv`), commuting with restriction
    25	  (`gluedTriv_res`), with the cross-piece comparison `gluedTriv_eq_unit_mul`
    26	  (`triv_i = g i j · triv_j` on opens below both pieces — the m-chart mirror of
    27	  `twistTriv₀_inf_eq`).
    28	
    29	The quasi-coherence packaging on a chart covered by finitely many basic-open pieces
    30	(DAT-1 stage 1b) is in `AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.GluedSheafQcoh`.
    31	
    32	## Implementation notes
    33	
    34	Sections are a genuine `Submodule` of the product of section modules (no defect map: the
    35	m-chart defect target would be a product-of-products); every element computation is
    36	`Scheme.resHom` bookkeeping, and restriction-path independence is definitional by proof
    37	irrelevance of `≤` after `Scheme.resHom_resHom` collapse. The sheaf condition glues each
    38	component in the structure sheaf of `k`-modules over the covers `{Wₐ ⊓ U j}ₐ` and checks
    39	the matching relation locally, mirroring `isSheaf_twistPresheaf`. The `k`-module
    40	structure on section modules is `Scheme.overModule`, activated locally per the house
    41	rule; `k` is an explicit argument throughout.
    42	-/

    58	/-- The double overlap `W ⊓ U i ⊓ U j` is contained in the second piece part `W ⊓ U j`. -/
    59	lemma gluedInclSnd (W : X.Opens) (i j : J) : W ⊓ U i ⊓ U j ≤ W ⊓ U j :=
    60	  le_inf (inf_le_left.trans inf_le_left) inf_le_right
    61	
    62	/-- The double overlap `W ⊓ U i ⊓ U j` is contained in the multiplier's home
    63	`U i ⊓ U j`. -/
    64	lemma gluedInclCoc (W : X.Opens) (i j : J) : W ⊓ U i ⊓ U j ≤ U i ⊓ U j :=

    70	
    71	/-- **The gluing cocycle law** for a family of transition units
    72	`g i j ∈ Γ(X, U i ⊓ U j)ˣ`: the normalization `g i i = 1` and the cocycle identity
    73	`g i j · g j l = g i l` as an equality in the triple-overlap section ring
    74	`Γ(X, U i ⊓ U j ⊓ U l)`. A `Prop`-mixin: the glued carrier (`gluedSubmodule`) needs no
    75	law; the piece trivializations (`gluedTriv`) consume it. -/
    76	structure Scheme.IsGluingCocycle {X : Scheme.{u}} {J : Type u} (U : J → X.Opens)
    77	    (g : ∀ i j : J, Γ(X, U i ⊓ U j)ˣ) : Prop where
    78	  /-- The diagonal units are `1`. -/
    79	  unit_self : ∀ i : J, (g i i : Γ(X, U i ⊓ U i)) = 1
    80	  /-- The cocycle identity on the triple overlap `U i ⊓ U j ⊓ U l`. -/
    81	  mul_res : ∀ i j l : J,
    82	    X.resHom (inf_le_left : U i ⊓ U j ⊓ U l ≤ U i ⊓ U j) (g i j : Γ(X, U i ⊓ U j)) *
    83	        X.resHom (gluedInclCoc U (U i) j l) (g j l : Γ(X, U j ⊓ U l)) =
    84	      X.resHom (gluedInclSnd U (U i) j l) (g i l : Γ(X, U i ⊓ U l))
    85	
    86	/-- The cocycle identity restricted to any open below the triple overlap. -/
    87	lemma Scheme.IsGluingCocycle.mul_res_of_le {X : Scheme.{u}} {J : Type u}
    88	    {U : J → X.Opens} {g : ∀ i j : J, Γ(X, U i ⊓ U j)ˣ} (hc : Scheme.IsGluingCocycle U g)
    89	    {i j l : J} {O : X.Opens} (hO : O ≤ U i ⊓ U j ⊓ U l) :
    90	    X.resHom (hO.trans (inf_le_left : U i ⊓ U j ⊓ U l ≤ U i ⊓ U j))
    91	          (g i j : Γ(X, U i ⊓ U j)) *
    92	        X.resHom (hO.trans (gluedInclCoc U (U i) j l)) (g j l : Γ(X, U j ⊓ U l)) =
    93	      X.resHom (hO.trans (gluedInclSnd U (U i) j l)) (g i l : Γ(X, U i ⊓ U l)) := by
    94	  have key := congrArg (X.resHom hO) (hc.mul_res i j l)
    95	  rw [map_mul] at key
    96	  simp only [Scheme.resHom_resHom] at key
    97	  exact key

   116	    c * (r • s) = r • (c * s) := by

   234	charts cover the curve and each chart is covered by its basic-open pieces. -/
   235	lemma exists_mem_pieces (x : relCurve C B) : ∃ j : D.index, x ∈ D.pieces j := by
   236	  have hx : x ∈ (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ ⊔ (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ := by
   237	    rw [relCover_sup]
   238	    trivial

   240	  · have hcov := D.cover₀ h0
   241	    rw [TopologicalSpace.Opens.mem_iSup] at hcov
   242	    obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := hcov
   243	    exact ⟨Sum.inl j, hj⟩
   244	  · have hcov := D.cover₁ h1
   245	    rw [TopologicalSpace.Opens.mem_iSup] at hcov
   246	    obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := hcov

      "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts \u2014 propose to the human instead).\n\nSTANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.\n\nWHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:\n- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.\n- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P \u2192 P`.\n- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.\n\nCOMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once. Write risky proofs as explicit `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`.",

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0RankOneLocus

/-!
# The native module carried by a glued rank-one datum

`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.sheaf` is already a sheaf of modules over the coefficient
ring.  The presentation contract also asks for the same object as a sheaf of
modules over the structure sheaf of the relative curve.  This file supplies
that bridge: the componentwise `gluedQsmul` action gives a module on every open,
`gluedRes_gluedQsmul` gives the semilinearity needed by
`PresheafOfModules.ofPresheaf`, and `gluedQsmul_overAlgebraMap` identifies its
restriction to the coefficient ring with the original datum sheaf.

This is deliberately only the native-module bridge.  It does not assert
`IsLineBundle`, pushforward base-change, or existence of a tied
`PicRankOneLocalPresentation`; those remain genuine producer obligations.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite TopologicalSpace

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom pi]

namespace BasicOpenCocycleDatum

noncomputable section

variable (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)

/-- The structure-sheaf module on the sections of the glued datum over one open.

The action is the componentwise multiplication action; the four module laws
are inherited from the corresponding `gluedQsmul` identities. -/
@[reducible] noncomputable def moduleOn (U : (relCurve C B).Opens) :
    Module Γ(relCurve C B, U)
      ((D.sheaf.obj ⋙ (forget₂ (ModuleCat B) AddCommGrpCat)).obj (op U)) := by
  change Module Γ(relCurve C B, U)
    (↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit U))
  letI : SMul Γ(relCurve C B, U)
      (↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit U)) :=
    ⟨fun r s => gluedQsmul B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : U ≤ U) r s⟩
  exact Module.ofMinimalAxioms
    (fun r x y => gluedQsmul_add B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : U ≤ U) r x y)
    (fun r s x => gluedQsmul_add_left B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : U ≤ U) r s x)
    (fun r s x => gluedQsmul_mul B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : U ≤ U) r s x)
    (fun x => gluedQsmul_one B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : U ≤ U) x)

/-- The presheaf of structure-sheaf modules underlying `D`. -/
noncomputable def nativePresheaf : (relCurve C B).PresheafOfModules := by
  let M : (relCurve C B).Opensᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat :=
    D.sheaf.obj ⋙ (forget₂ (ModuleCat B) AddCommGrpCat)
  let family : ∀ U : (relCurve C B).Opensᵒᵖ,
      Module ((relCurve C B).ringCatSheaf.obj.obj U) (M.obj U) :=
    fun U => moduleOn D U.unop
  letI : ∀ U : (relCurve C B).Opensᵒᵖ,
      Module ((relCurve C B).ringCatSheaf.obj.obj U) (M.obj U) := family
  exact PresheafOfModules.ofPresheaf M (by
    intro X Y f r m
    change gluedRes B D.pieces D.unit f.unop.le
        (gluedQsmul B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : X.unop ≤ X.unop) r m) =
      gluedQsmul B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : Y.unop ≤ Y.unop)
        ((relCurve C B).resHom f.unop.le r)
        (gluedRes B D.pieces D.unit f.unop.le m)
    rw [gluedRes_gluedQsmul]
    apply Subtype.ext
    funext j
    rw [gluedQsmul_coe, gluedQsmul_coe]
    simp only [Scheme.resHom_resHom])

/-- The native `Scheme.Modules` object associated to a glued datum. -/
noncomputable def nativeModule : (relCurve C B).Modules := by
  refine ⟨nativePresheaf D, ?_⟩
  rw [show (nativePresheaf D).presheaf =
    D.sheaf.obj ⋙ (forget₂ (ModuleCat B) AddCommGrpCat) from rfl]
  rw [Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_forget _ _
    (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u})]
  convert (Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_forget _ _
    (CategoryTheory.forget (ModuleCat.{u} B))).mp D.sheaf.property using 1
  all_goals rfl

/-- On every open, restricting `D.nativeModule` to the coefficient ring recovers
the datum's original module of sections.

The equivalence is the identity on sections. Its linearity is the substantive
point: `gluedQsmul_overAlgebraMap` identifies the native structure-sheaf action
of a coefficient scalar with the datum's coefficient action. -/
noncomputable def nativeModuleKSectionsEquiv
    (U : (relCurve C B).Opens) :
    (Scheme.toModuleKSheafOfModules
      (Over.mk (relCurve C B ↘ Spec (.of B))) (nativeModule D)).obj.obj (op U) ≃ₗ[B]
      D.sheaf.obj.obj (op U) := by
  let f :
      (Scheme.toModuleKSheafOfModules
        (Over.mk (relCurve C B ↘ Spec (.of B))) (nativeModule D)).obj.obj (op U) →ₗ[B]
        D.sheaf.obj.obj (op U) :=
    { toFun := fun x => x
      map_add' := by
        intros
        rfl
      map_smul' := by
        intro r x
        change gluedQsmul B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : U ≤ U)
            ((relCurve C B).overAlgebraMap B U r) x =
          r • (show D.sheaf.obj.obj (op U) from x)
        exact gluedQsmul_overAlgebraMap B D.pieces D.unit
          (le_rfl : U ≤ U) r x }
  exact LinearEquiv.ofBijective f ⟨fun _ _ h => h, fun y => ⟨y, rfl⟩⟩

/-- The base-ring sheaf of `D.nativeModule` is canonically the datum sheaf.

This has exactly the type of `PicRankOneLocalPresentation.module_iso` when the
presentation's native module is chosen to be `D.nativeModule`. -/
noncomputable def nativeModuleKSheafIso :
    Scheme.toModuleKSheafOfModules
      (Over.mk (relCurve C B ↘ Spec (.of B))) (nativeModule D) ≅ D.sheaf :=
  (fullyFaithfulSheafToPresheaf _ _).preimageIso
    (NatIso.ofComponents
      (fun U => (nativeModuleKSectionsEquiv D U.unop).toModuleIso)

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0RankOneLocusNative

/-!
# The canonical native rank-one presentation contract

`PicRankOneLocalPresentation` deliberately leaves the geometric producer fields explicit.
This file fixes the module part of that contract: for a tied cocycle datum `D`, the module is
always `D.nativeModule` and its base-ring comparison is always
`D.nativeModuleKSheafIso`.  The remaining fields (`IsLineBundle`, arbitrary-cartesian
pushforward base change, and the cohomology/rank certificates) stay as explicit obligations.

The resulting contract is therefore an adapter interface for a future producer, rather than a
second choice of a line bundle.  Its conversion is consumed directly by the public
`PicRankOneOpen` membership theorem below; no unrelated module or untied class can enter
through this bridge, and the adapter itself does not provide the geometric certificates.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite MonoidalCategory
  CartesianMonoidalCategory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]

/-! ## The native adapter contract -/

/--
A lambda-tied rank-one presentation whose module is canonically the native module of its
cocycle datum.

The fields after `datum_class` are exactly the obligations which are absent from the native
glued-sheaf bridge.  Keeping them explicit prevents a field-level H⁰/H¹ calculation or an
unrelated line bundle from being silently substituted for the native evaluation module.
-/
structure PicRankOneNativePresentation
    (lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)) : Type (u + 1) where
  cover : Algebra.EtaleCover A
  representative : descentClasses C cover
  represents :
    PicEtAff.mk C cover representative = picEtAffineEquiv C A lam.1
  datum : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C cover.Carrier pi
  datum_class :
    (representative : relPic C (overSpec k cover.Carrier)) =
      relPicMk C (overSpec k cover.Carrier) datum.cechPicClass
  line_bundle : Scheme.Modules.IsLineBundle datum.nativeModule
  native_pushforward_base_change :
    ∀ {T' X' : Scheme.{u}}
      (g : T' ⟶ Spec (.of cover.Carrier)) (f' : X' ⟶ T')
      (g' : X' ⟶ relCurve C cover.Carrier)
      (sq : IsPullback g' f'
        (relCurve C cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of cover.Carrier)) g),
      IsIso ((canonicalBaseChangeMap sq).app datum.nativeModule)
  h1_vanishing : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 1)
  h0_finite : Module.Finite cover.Carrier (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 0)
  h0_projective : Module.Projective cover.Carrier (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 0)
  h0_rank_one :
    ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum cover.Carrier,
      Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 0) p = 1

namespace PicRankOneNativePresentation

variable {pi} {lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)}

/-- Convert the native adapter contract to the existing local-presentation contract.

The two native bridge fields are inserted definitionally; all other fields are transported
without weakening or adding hypotheses.
-/
noncomputable def toLocalPresentation
    (P : PicRankOneNativePresentation pi lam) :
    PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam :=
  { cover := P.cover
    representative := P.representative
    represents := P.represents
    datum := P.datum
    datum_class := P.datum_class
    module := P.datum.nativeModule
    module_iso := P.datum.nativeModuleKSheafIso
    line_bundle := P.line_bundle
    native_pushforward_base_change := P.native_pushforward_base_change
    h1_vanishing := P.h1_vanishing
    h0_finite := P.h0_finite
    h0_projective := P.h0_projective
    h0_rank_one := P.h0_rank_one }

theorem nonempty_localPresentation
    (P : PicRankOneNativePresentation pi lam) :
    Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam) :=
  ⟨P.toLocalPresentation⟩

end PicRankOneNativePresentation

/-! ## Immediate rank-one-locus consumer -/

/--
An arbitrary-affine family of native contracts supplies the existing public rank-one-locus
consumer.  The family is quantified in exactly the same way as
`PicRankOneOpen.LocalPresentationCondition`; the conversion only canonicalizes the module
choice and does not manufacture any of the remaining geometric certificates.
-/
theorem mem_picRankOneOpen_of_nativePresentations
    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
    (h : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
        (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
        Nonempty (PicRankOneNativePresentation pi
          ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))) :
    lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T := by
  apply mem_picRankOneOpen_of_localPresentations pi
  intro A _ _ t
  obtain ⟨P⟩ := h A t
  exact P.nonempty_localPresentation

end AlgebraicGeometry

In this file, we define the abelian category of sheaves of modules
`X.Modules` over a scheme `X`, and study its basic functoriality.

variable (X) in
/-- The category of sheaves of modules over a scheme. -/
def Modules := SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf

namespace Modules

/-- Morphisms between `𝒪ₓ`-modules. Use `Hom.app` to act on sections. -/
def Hom (M N : X.Modules) : Type u := SheafOfModules.Hom M N

instance : Category X.Modules where
  Hom := Modules.Hom
  __ := (inferInstance : Category (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf))

noncomputable instance : Abelian X.Modules :=
  inferInstanceAs <| Abelian (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf)
instance : HasLimits X.Modules := inferInstanceAs (HasLimits (SheafOfModules X.ringCatSheaf))
instance : HasColimits X.Modules := inferInstanceAs (HasColimits (SheafOfModules X.ringCatSheaf))

/-- The forgetful functor from `𝒪ₓ`-modules to presheaves of modules.
This is mostly useful to transport results from (pre)sheaves of modules to `𝒪ₓ`-modules and
usually shouldn't be used directly when working with actual `𝒪ₓ`-modules. -/
def toPresheafOfModules : X.Modules ⥤ X.PresheafOfModules := SheafOfModules.forget _

/-- The forgetful functor from `𝒪ₓ`-modules to presheaves of modules is fully faithful. -/
def fullyFaithfulToPresheafOfModules : (Modules.toPresheafOfModules X).FullyFaithful :=
  SheafOfModules.fullyFaithfulForget _

instance : (toPresheafOfModules X).Full := fullyFaithfulToPresheafOfModules.full

module

public import Mathlib.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.ChangeOfRings
public import Mathlib.Algebra.Category.Ring.Basic

/-!
# Presheaves of modules over a presheaf of rings.

Given a presheaf of rings `R : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat`, we define the category `PresheafOfModules R`.
An object `M : PresheafOfModules R` consists of a family of modules
`M.obj X : ModuleCat (R.obj X)` for all `X : Cᵒᵖ`, together with the data, for all `f : X ⟶ Y`,
of a functorial linear map `M.map f` from `M.obj X` to the restriction
of scalars of `M.obj Y` via `R.map f`.


## Future work

* Compare this to the definition as a presheaf of pairs `(R, M)` with specified first part.
* Compare this to the definition as a module object of the presheaf of rings
  thought of as a monoid object.
* Presheaves of modules over a presheaf of commutative rings form a monoidal category.
* Pushforward and pullback.
-/

@[expose] public section

universe v v₁ u₁ u

open CategoryTheory LinearMap Opposite

variable {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C] {R : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{u}}

variable (R) in
/-- A presheaf of modules over `R : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat` consists of family of
objects `obj X : ModuleCat (R.obj X)` for all `X : Cᵒᵖ` together with
functorial maps `obj X ⟶ (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (R.map f)).obj (obj Y)`
for all `f : X ⟶ Y` in `Cᵒᵖ`. -/
structure PresheafOfModules where
  /-- a family of modules over `R.obj X` for all `X` -/
  obj (X : Cᵒᵖ) : ModuleCat.{v} (R.obj X)
  /-- the restriction maps of a presheaf of modules -/
  map {X Y : Cᵒᵖ} (f : X ⟶ Y) : obj X ⟶ (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (R.map f).hom).obj (obj Y)
  map_id (X : Cᵒᵖ) :
    map (𝟙 X) = (ModuleCat.restrictScalarsId' (R.map (𝟙 X)).hom
      (congrArg RingCat.Hom.hom (R.map_id X))).inv.app _ := by
        cat_disch
  map_comp {X Y Z : Cᵒᵖ} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) :
    map (f ≫ g) = map f ≫ (ModuleCat.restrictScalars _).map (map g) ≫
      (ModuleCat.restrictScalarsComp' (R.map f).hom (R.map g).hom (R.map (f ≫ g)).hom
        (congrArg RingCat.Hom.hom <| R.map_comp f g)).inv.app _ := by cat_disch

namespace PresheafOfModules

attribute [simp] map_id map_comp
attribute [reassoc] map_comp

#adaptation_note /-- https://github.com/leanprover/lean4/pull/12564
This is required for `Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Differentials.Presheaf` -/
instance {R : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}} (X : Cᵒᵖ) (M : PresheafOfModules.{v} (R ⋙ forget₂ _ _)) :
    Module (R.obj X) (M.obj X) := (M.obj X).isModule

variable (M M₁ M₂ : PresheafOfModules.{v} R)

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
protected lemma map_smul {X Y : Cᵒᵖ} (f : X ⟶ Y) (r : R.obj X) (m : M.obj X) :
    M.map f (r • m) = R.map f r • M.map f m := by simp

lemma congr_map_apply {X Y : Cᵒᵖ} {f g : X ⟶ Y} (h : f = g) (m : M.obj X) :
    M.map f m = M.map g m := by rw [h]

lemma map_comp_apply {U V W : Cᵒᵖ} (i : U ⟶ V) (j : V ⟶ W) (x) :
    M.map (i ≫ j) x = M.map j (M.map i x) := by
  rw [M.map_comp]; rfl

/-- A morphism of presheaves of modules consists of a family of linear maps which
satisfy the naturality condition. -/
@[ext]
structure Hom where
  /-- a family of linear maps `M₁.obj X ⟶ M₂.obj X` for all `X`. -/
  app (X : Cᵒᵖ) : M₁.obj X ⟶ M₂.obj X
  naturality {X Y : Cᵒᵖ} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
      M₁.map f ≫ (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (R.map f).hom).map (app Y) =
        app X ≫ M₂.map f := by cat_disch

attribute [reassoc (attr := simp)] Hom.naturality

instance : Category (PresheafOfModules.{v} R) where
  Hom := Hom
  id _ := { app := fun _ ↦ 𝟙 _ }
  comp f g := { app := fun _ ↦ f.app _ ≫ g.app _ }

variable {M₁ M₂}

@[ext]
lemma hom_ext {f g : M₁ ⟶ M₂} (h : ∀ (X : Cᵒᵖ), f.app X = g.app X) :
    f = g := Hom.ext (by ext1; apply h)

@[simp]
lemma id_app (M : PresheafOfModules R) (X : Cᵒᵖ) : Hom.app (𝟙 M) X = 𝟙 _ := by
  rfl

@[simp]
lemma comp_app {M₁ M₂ M₃ : PresheafOfModules R} (f : M₁ ⟶ M₂) (g : M₂ ⟶ M₃) (X : Cᵒᵖ) :
    (f ≫ g).app X = f.app X ≫ g.app X := by
  rfl

lemma naturality_apply (f : M₁ ⟶ M₂) {X Y : Cᵒᵖ} (g : X ⟶ Y) (x : M₁.obj X) :
    Hom.app f Y (M₁.map g x) = M₂.map g (Hom.app f X x) :=
  CategoryTheory.congr_fun (Hom.naturality f g) x

/-- Constructor for isomorphisms in the category of presheaves of modules. -/
@[simps!]
def isoMk (app : ∀ (X : Cᵒᵖ), M₁.obj X ≅ M₂.obj X)
    (naturality : ∀ ⦃X Y : Cᵒᵖ⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y),
      M₁.map f ≫ (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (R.map f).hom).map (app Y).hom =
        (app X).hom ≫ M₂.map f := by cat_disch) : M₁ ≅ M₂ where
  hom := { app := fun X ↦ (app X).hom }
  inv :=
    { app := fun X ↦ (app X).inv
      naturality := fun {X Y} f ↦ by
        rw [← cancel_epi (app X).hom, ← reassoc_of% (naturality f), Iso.map_hom_inv_id,
          Category.comp_id, Iso.hom_inv_id_assoc] }

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
/-- The underlying presheaf of abelian groups of a presheaf of modules. -/
noncomputable def presheaf : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Ab where
  obj X := (forget₂ _ _).obj (M.obj X)
  map f := AddCommGrpCat.ofHom <| AddMonoidHom.mk' (M.map f) (by simp)

@[simp]
lemma presheaf_obj_coe (X : Cᵒᵖ) :
    (M.presheaf.obj X : Type _) = M.obj X := rfl

@[simp]
lemma presheaf_map_apply_coe {X Y : Cᵒᵖ} (f : X ⟶ Y) (x : M.obj X) :
    DFunLike.coe (α := M.obj X) (β := fun _ ↦ M.obj Y) (M.presheaf.map f).hom x = M.map f x := rfl

instance (M : PresheafOfModules R) (X : Cᵒᵖ) :
    Module (R.obj X) (M.presheaf.obj X) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Module (R.obj X) (M.obj X))

variable (R) in
/-- The forgetful functor `PresheafOfModules R ⥤ Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Ab`. -/
noncomputable def toPresheaf : PresheafOfModules.{v} R ⥤ Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Ab where
  obj M := M.presheaf
  map f :=

/-!
# The m-chart cocycle-glued sheaf (DAT-1, stage 1a)

For a scheme `X` over `Spec k`, a family of opens `U : J → X.Opens` and **transition
multipliers** `g i j ∈ Γ(X, U i ⊓ U j)ˣ`, the glued sheaf of `informal/spec-dat-1.md`
(the m-chart generalization of the two-chart `AlgebraicGeometry.twistSheaf`), as a sheaf
of `k`-modules on the small Zariski site of `X`:
`F_g(W) = {s ∈ Π j, Γ(W ⊓ U j) | s i = g i j · s j on W ⊓ U i ⊓ U j for all i, j}`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.gluedSheaf`), together with

* the **cocycle law** `Scheme.IsGluingCocycle` (`g i i = 1` and
  `g i j · g j l = g i l` on triple overlaps) — a `Prop`-structure: the carrier needs no
  law (the matching relation is restriction-stable for arbitrary multipliers), the
  trivializations consume it;
* the **piece trivializations** `F_g(W) ≃ₗ[k] Γ(X, W)` for `W ≤ U j`, given by the
  `j`-th component (`AlgebraicGeometry.gluedTriv`), commuting with restriction
  (`gluedTriv_res`), with the cross-piece comparison `gluedTriv_eq_unit_mul`
  (`triv_i = g i j · triv_j` on opens below both pieces — the m-chart mirror of
  `twistTriv₀_inf_eq`).

The quasi-coherence packaging on a chart covered by finitely many basic-open pieces
(DAT-1 stage 1b) is in `AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.GluedSheafQcoh`.

## Implementation notes

Sections are a genuine `Submodule` of the product of section modules (no defect map: the
m-chart defect target would be a product-of-products); every element computation is
`Scheme.resHom` bookkeeping, and restriction-path independence is definitional by proof
irrelevance of `≤` after `Scheme.resHom_resHom` collapse. The sheaf condition glues each
component in the structure sheaf of `k`-modules over the covers `{Wₐ ⊓ U j}ₐ` and checks
the matching relation locally, mirroring `isSheaf_twistPresheaf`. The `k`-module
structure on section modules is `Scheme.overModule`, activated locally per the house
rule; `k` is an explicit argument throughout.
-/

/-! ## The inclusion lattice of the pieces -/

section Incl

variable {X : Scheme.{u}} {J : Type u} (U : J → X.Opens)

/-- The double overlap `W ⊓ U i ⊓ U j` is contained in the second piece part `W ⊓ U j`. -/
lemma gluedInclSnd (W : X.Opens) (i j : J) : W ⊓ U i ⊓ U j ≤ W ⊓ U j :=
  le_inf (inf_le_left.trans inf_le_left) inf_le_right

/-- The double overlap `W ⊓ U i ⊓ U j` is contained in the multiplier's home
`U i ⊓ U j`. -/
lemma gluedInclCoc (W : X.Opens) (i j : J) : W ⊓ U i ⊓ U j ≤ U i ⊓ U j :=
  le_inf (inf_le_left.trans inf_le_right) inf_le_right

end Incl

/-! ## The cocycle law -/

/-- **The gluing cocycle law** for a family of transition units
`g i j ∈ Γ(X, U i ⊓ U j)ˣ`: the normalization `g i i = 1` and the cocycle identity
`g i j · g j l = g i l` as an equality in the triple-overlap section ring
`Γ(X, U i ⊓ U j ⊓ U l)`. A `Prop`-mixin: the glued carrier (`gluedSubmodule`) needs no
law; the piece trivializations (`gluedTriv`) consume it. -/
structure Scheme.IsGluingCocycle {X : Scheme.{u}} {J : Type u} (U : J → X.Opens)
    (g : ∀ i j : J, Γ(X, U i ⊓ U j)ˣ) : Prop where
  /-- The diagonal units are `1`. -/
  unit_self : ∀ i : J, (g i i : Γ(X, U i ⊓ U i)) = 1
  /-- The cocycle identity on the triple overlap `U i ⊓ U j ⊓ U l`. -/
  mul_res : ∀ i j l : J,
    X.resHom (inf_le_left : U i ⊓ U j ⊓ U l ≤ U i ⊓ U j) (g i j : Γ(X, U i ⊓ U j)) *
        X.resHom (gluedInclCoc U (U i) j l) (g j l : Γ(X, U j ⊓ U l)) =
      X.resHom (gluedInclSnd U (U i) j l) (g i l : Γ(X, U i ⊓ U l))

/-- The cocycle identity restricted to any open below the triple overlap. -/
lemma Scheme.IsGluingCocycle.mul_res_of_le {X : Scheme.{u}} {J : Type u}
    {U : J → X.Opens} {g : ∀ i j : J, Γ(X, U i ⊓ U j)ˣ} (hc : Scheme.IsGluingCocycle U g)
    {i j l : J} {O : X.Opens} (hO : O ≤ U i ⊓ U j ⊓ U l) :
    X.resHom (hO.trans (inf_le_left : U i ⊓ U j ⊓ U l ≤ U i ⊓ U j))
          (g i j : Γ(X, U i ⊓ U j)) *
        X.resHom (hO.trans (gluedInclCoc U (U i) j l)) (g j l : Γ(X, U j ⊓ U l)) =
      X.resHom (hO.trans (gluedInclSnd U (U i) j l)) (g i l : Γ(X, U i ⊓ U l)) := by
  have key := congrArg (X.resHom hO) (hc.mul_res i j l)
  rw [map_mul] at key
  simp only [Scheme.resHom_resHom] at key
  exact key

/-- The matching relation is stable under componentwise restriction. -/
lemma gluedSubmodule_res {W' W : X.Opens} (h : W' ≤ W)
    {s : ∀ j : J, Γ(X, W ⊓ U j)} (hs : s ∈ gluedSubmodule k U g W) :
    (fun j => X.resHom (inf_le_inf_right (U j) h) (s j)) ∈ gluedSubmodule k U g W' := by
  intro i j
  have key := congrArg
    (X.resHom (inf_le_inf_right (U j) (inf_le_inf_right (U i) h) :
      W' ⊓ U i ⊓ U j ≤ W ⊓ U i ⊓ U j)) (hs i j)
  rw [map_mul] at key
  simp only [Scheme.resHom_resHom] at key ⊢
  exact key

/-- Componentwise restriction of glued sections, as a `k`-linear map. -/
noncomputable def gluedRes {W' W : X.Opens} (h : W' ≤ W) :
    ↥(gluedSubmodule k U g W) →ₗ[k] ↥(gluedSubmodule k U g W') :=
  LinearMap.restrict
    (LinearMap.pi fun j => (secRes (X.moduleKSheaf k) (inf_le_inf_right (U j) h)).comp
      (LinearMap.proj j))
    (fun _ hs => gluedSubmodule_res k U g h hs)

  rfl

/-- Restriction of an `𝒪ₓ`-module along an open immersion.

def restrictFunctor : Y.Modules ⥤ X.Modules :=
  letI α : X.presheaf ⟶ f.opensFunctor.op ⋙ Y.presheaf := { app U := (f.appIso U.unop).inv }
  SheafOfModules.pushforward (F := f.opensFunctor)
    ⟨Functor.whiskerRight α (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)⟩

abbrev restrict (M : Y.Modules) (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsOpenImmersion f] : X.Modules :=
  (restrictFunctor f).obj M

def restrictAppIso (M : Y.Modules) (U : X.Opens) : Γ(M.restrict f, U) ≅ Γ(M, f ''ᵁ U) :=

# Pushforward of sheaves of modules

Assume that categories `C` and `D` are equipped with Grothendieck topologies, and
that `F : C ⥤ D` is a continuous functor.
Then, if `φ : S ⟶ (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{u} J K).obj R` is
a morphism of sheaves of rings, we construct the pushforward functor
`pushforward φ : SheafOfModules.{v} R ⥤ SheafOfModules.{v} S`, and
we show that they interact with the composition of morphisms similarly as pseudofunctors.

-/

/-- The pushforward of sheaves of modules that is induced by a continuous functor `F`
and a morphism of sheaves of rings `φ : S ⟶ (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat J K).obj R`. -/
@[simps map_val, simps -isSimp obj_val]
noncomputable def pushforward : SheafOfModules.{v} R ⥤ SheafOfModules.{v} S where
  obj M :=
    { val := (PresheafOfModules.pushforward φ.hom).obj M.val
      isSheaf := ((F.sheafPushforwardContinuous _ J K).obj ⟨_, M.isSheaf⟩).property }
  map f :=
    { val := (PresheafOfModules.pushforward φ.hom).map f.val }

/-- The restriction functor from sheaves of `R`-modules to sheaves of `R.over X`-modules

  pushforward (𝟙 _)

noncomputable abbrev over (M : SheafOfModules.{v} R) (X : D) : SheafOfModules.{v} (R.over X) :=
  (overFunctor R X).obj M

/-- Given a map `f : M ⟶ N` between sheaves of modules over `R`, this is the restriction

noncomputable abbrev Hom.over {M N : SheafOfModules.{v} R} (f : M ⟶ N) (X : D) :
